question: If 3ⁿ = 243, what will be the value of (1)⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify that **243** is the **5th** power of **3** (3⁵ = 243), so **n = 5**.

The expression to find is **(1)⁽ⁿ−¹⁾**.

Since the base is **1**, any real power applied to it will result in **1**.

**∴ 1⁽⁵−¹⁾ = 1⁴ = 1**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3ⁿ = 243

**Formula Used:**

If **am = aⁿ**, then **m = n** (for a > 0, a ≠ 1).

**1k = 1** for any real value of **k**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3ⁿ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3

⇒ 3ⁿ = 3⁵

⇒ **n = 5**

⇒ Required value = (1)⁽ⁿ−¹⁾

⇒ Required value = (1)⁽⁵−¹⁾

⇒ Required value = 1⁴

⇒ Required value = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Laws of Indices

When the bases are identical on both sides of an equation, their **exponents** must be equal: **am = aⁿ ⇒ m = n**.

Power of Unity

The number **1** is the multiplicative identity; raising it to any **finite power** always results in **1** (1ⁿ = 1).

Zero Exponent Rule

Any non-zero base raised to the power of **zero** is equal to **1** (a⁰ = 1, where a ≠ 0).
